messages.content: Salt Lake is done and I’m back at my desk. The Chicago pediatric therapy conference packet finally landed: conference Sept. 19-21, panel Friday morning, lab Saturday afternoon, optional Sunday breakfast. Can you start the travel comparison?

Yes. I’ll frame it around arriving Thursday and returning Sunday afternoon unless the schedule pushes us another way. Are we only comparing for now, or should I hold anything if the block is about to close?

Compare only for the moment. Group it by what is practical, not just cheapest. I’ll have lab notes and a small materials bag, so daily schlepping matters. A room with coffee and a fridge would help, and call out pool/hot tub/fitness gaps.

Flight pattern I’d lead with: TPA to ORD nonstop Thursday Sept. 18 around 9:20 a.m., landing 11:05 a.m.; return ORD to TPA Sunday around 2:40 p.m., landing about 6:20 p.m. It is pricing around $336 round-trip in regular economy, with seat selection available. It gives you a real cushion before any Thursday presenter check-in and avoids a late Sunday night.
What about Midway? I don’t mind it if the savings are meaningful.

Midway is only saving about $35 to $50 on the flight options I’m seeing. It adds more crosstown time to the conference hotel and leaves fewer easy fallbacks if the Sunday breakfast runs long. If the fare gap grows, it could be worth revisiting, but today ORD is the cleaner choice.
Okay, hotels. Official hotel versus the suite property nearby.

Two clear candidates. Official hotel is Lakeside Grand Chicago, connected to the meeting space: $239/night in the block, Google rating 4.4, standard queen, coffee maker, fitness room, indoor pool. Mini-fridges are by request only, and there is no hot tub. Nearby suite option is State Street Suites: about a 12-15 minute walk or short rideshare, $268/night, Google rating 4.3, queen studio with coffee maker and mini-fridge, plus pool, hot tub, and fitness room.
The fridge request is the annoying part. Do they charge for it or just say maybe?

The official hotel says there is no fee, but it is inventory-limited and not guaranteed until room assignment. Conference sales can attach it as a presenter request. The suite hotel guarantees it because it is part of the studio setup.
For the lab, do we know whether I’m hauling materials back and forth?

Not yet. The packet says presenter check-in will be Thursday afternoon and the Saturday lab has assigned materials, but it does not confirm storage, Friday room access, or teardown timing. That answer matters: if meeting-space storage is confirmed, the connected hotel becomes much stronger.
Cancellation timing? I don’t want a fake bargain that traps us earlier.

Plain version: the official block must be reserved by Aug. 15, then can be canceled until Sept. 15 at 6 p.m. Central before a one-night penalty. State Street Suites is more expensive and has a stricter seven-day cancellation cutoff. So the suite has better room amenities but less flexibility and more movement.
Give me the practical stack.

First choice if the conference confirms storage and the fridge request can be attached: ORD flights plus Lakeside Grand. It is not the most amenity-complete, but it minimizes daily movement and protects the panel/lab schedule. Second choice: ORD plus State Street Suites if guaranteed fridge and hot tub matter more than the connected location. Third: Midway flights with either hotel only if the savings become much bigger.
Sunday return after the networking breakfast: does the 2:40 ORD flight make me leave rudely early?

No. If breakfast runs 8:00-9:30, you could check out, leave bags, have a buffer conversation, and still leave the hotel around 11:30 or 11:45 for ORD. A noon flight would be rushed; 2:40 is the workable middle ground.
Can you put anything on hold without actually booking?

The official block does not offer a courtesy hold; it becomes a cancellable reservation as soon as we enter the card. Same with the suite. I can save both live links, set the block-deadline reminder, and send the conference office the missing questions before you commit.
Do that. Save the official as the leading option and the suite as backup. No booking yet.

Saved only, no booking. I set a fare watch for the Thursday morning ORD outbound and Sunday afternoon ORD return. I saved Lakeside Grand as the practical lead with notes: queen room, coffee maker, fridge request only, indoor pool, fitness room, no hot tub, cancel by Sept. 15 if booked before the block deadline. State Street Suites is saved as the backup with guaranteed fridge, pool, hot tub, fitness, higher total cost, and more daily movement. I also sent the conference office questions on presenter check-in, Friday room access, Saturday lab storage, teardown timing, fridge priority, and the easiest ORD transit/load-in route.
